tier_justification: The first conjunct is the polarity Galois connection that every relation induces (textbook); the second is a corollary of `lower_best_iff`.
plain_claim: For every relation `P` between attributes and traces, `alphaOf P` and `gammaOf P` form a Galois connection in the imported sense with the reverse-inclusion order on attribute sets (`polarity_galois`); for every positive-size shape `s` (every `Shape` has `size_pos : 0 < size`) and position `pos`, the instance `alphaSet s pos`, `gammaDual s pos` (with `P = attrSat s pos`) is therefore a Galois connection, and for every modality `m`, `lower s pos m = (alphaSet s pos (denP s m)).val`. By contrast (`lower_no_left_adjoint_and_arg_no_right_adjoint`), for every shape `s` and position `pos` there is no function `u : AttrSet → Mod` with `A ≤ lower s pos m ↔ u A ≤ m` for all `m` and `A` (no left adjoint), neither over all modalities nor over `s`-closed ones, and there is no function `u : AttrSet → Mod` with `lower s .arg m ≤ A ↔ m ≤ u A` for all `m` and `A` (no right adjoint of the argument lowering over all modalities).
nonvacuity_witness: `ex_galois_defs`: instances of `AttrDual`, `gammaDual`, `denP` and `alphaSet s1 .arg (denP s1 refFull) = lower s1 .arg refFull`.
non_claims: The Galois connection is between predicates on traces and attribute sets; it holds for every relation (`polarity_galois`) and carries no content specific to modalities. Between modalities and attribute sets, `lower s pos` has no left adjoint (no `u` with `A ≤ lower s pos m ↔ u A ≤ m`), over all modalities and over `s`-closed modalities, and `lower s .arg` has no right adjoint (no `u` with `lower s .arg m ≤ A ↔ m ≤ u A`) over all modalities (`lower_no_left_adjoint_and_arg_no_right_adjoint`) and over `s`-closed modalities (`lower_arg_no_right_adjoint_on_closed`). `lower s .ret` has the right adjoint `retRightAdjoint`, with `s`-closed values, when `s.alignLog ≠ 0` (`lower_ret_right_adjoint_of_alignLog_ne_zero`), and no right adjoint, over all or over `s`-closed modalities, when `s.alignLog = 0` (`lower_ret_no_right_adjoint_of_alignLog_eq_zero`). The cited package's characterization of Galois connections (card `R1-gc-iff`) is stated for a reflexive and transitive abstract order; the reverse-inclusion order on `AttrDual` is reflexive and transitive (`attrDual_le_refl_trans`). Monotonicity, extensivity and reductivity are not re-proved here.

tier_justification: Concrete witnesses that a call-entry modality entails different attributes at call entry and at the return point: argument versus return `noalias`, and call-entry dereferenceability versus dereferenceability at the return point after a free during the call. plain_claim: For every type `τ` (whose pointer leaves `Ty.ptr s m` have positive-size shapes: every `Shape` has `size_pos : 0 < size`) and list of field paths `qs`: replacing a local of type `τ` by one local per field path in `qs`, each with the field's declared type (`scalarize τ qs`; paths that are not fields are skipped), is a refinement for all programs (`Refines`: every assertion pattern `P.asserts` and every assignment `P.exec` of call traces to asserted leaves) iff for every `q ∈ qs` with declared field type `σ` and every pointer leaf `p'` of `σ` whose modality computed inside `σ` is `m` (`modAt σ p' = some (s, m)`), `m ≤ posTrans τ q m`.

A program is an assertion pattern plus an assignment of traces (`Prog`), with no operational semantics; temporal lifetime transitions (a pointer valid when stored and invalidated later), movement or duplication of retag points, and partially initialized or dead fields are not modelled. tier_justification: The stop-at-relaxer policy mirrors the merged rustc change; the exclusion and retyping policies are toy alternatives, compared by proved acceptance inclusions.
plain_claim: For types whose pointer leaves have positive-size shapes (every `Shape` has `size_pos : 0 < size`), the exclusion policy `repairExclude`, the retyping policy `repairRetype` and the stop-at-relaxer policy `repairStopAtRelaxer` are each sound (`PolicySound`: every scalarization they return is a refinement for all programs), and `naivePolicy` is not; (`repairs_exact_and_retype_total`) all three are exact (`PolicyExact`: whenever the policy scalarizes a type `τ` with path list `qs` (`pol τ qs = some locals`), one new local per requested field path of `τ`, in order, and every pointer leaf of a new local has exactly the modality the same leaf has in `τ`), and `repairRetype` returns a scalarization for every type and path list; (`repair_policies_acceptance_hierarchy`) whenever `repairExclude` scalarizes, `repairStopAtRelaxer` returns the same locals, and whenever `repairStopAtRelaxer` scalarizes, `repairRetype` returns the same locals, both inclusions strict (`tyPairMD s1`; `tyMDPair s1` with `qsMDPair`), and `repairStopAtRelaxer` refuses `tyMDScalar` (`ManuallyDrop<u8>`) with paths `[[.inner]]` although that scalarization is a refinement.
nonvacuity_witness: `nv_repairs`: all three policies scalarize `(&mut T, u8)`, and `repairRetype` scalarizes the headline type.
non_claims: `PolicySound` alone admits degenerate policies: always refusing and always returning no locals are sound, and the latter is not exact (`policySound_degenerate`); exactness is the separate predicate `PolicyExact`, which implies soundness (`policySound_of_exact`). `PolicyExact` holds vacuously for the always-refusing policy, and it constrains the modalities of pointer leaves (`modAt`), not the scalar structure of the new locals: a policy that retypes scalar fields as pairs of scalars and otherwise behaves like `repairRetype` is exact (`policyExact_refusing_and_scalar_reshaping`).

`repairRetype` gives each new local under a relaxing wrapper the type `relaxAll σ`, whose pointer leaves have modality `tRelax m` (alignment and non-null promises kept; `modAt_retype`, `modAt_relaxAll`). If `m` keeps neither promise, so that `tRelax m = Mod.bot` (for example a raw pointer, `m = Mod.bot`), the new leaf has the raw-pointer modality `kindBase .raw`, which is `Mod.bot` by the definition of `kindBase`. If `tRelax m ≠ Mod.bot` (for example the base modality of a shared reference, a mutable reference or a box, which keeps alignment and non-null), then `tRelax m` is not the modality of any of the four documented pointer constructors (not proved here). How a compiler would express such a type is not examined.

`repairStopAtRelaxer` is more conservative than the exact condition of `scalarize_refines_iff_declared_le_posMod`: it refuses `tyMDScalar` with paths `[[.inner]]` although that scalarization refines (`repair_policies_acceptance_hierarchy`).

The correspondence between `repairStopAtRelaxer` and the merged rustc change (which excludes locals whose type satisfies `is_like_maybe_dangling()`) is a derived modelling bridge; the exclusion and retyping policies correspond to no cited rustc code.

Kernel dependency audit for `Shape.size_pos` (shapes have positive size by construction): the proofs of `repairs_sound`, `repair_policies_acceptance_hierarchy` use it, so zero-sized pointees are outside their scope and these statements neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims for them; the proof of `repairs_exact_and_retype_total` does not use it.
These are statements about the toy model; they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about rustc or LLVM. Model–system relation: none proved.
